findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can run before exceptions are recorded
findings.body: The test spawns a reader thread that polls `groups(...)` and records exceptions into `caughtExceptions`, then sets `deletedAll` and immediately asserts the list is empty. Because the thread is never joined, an exception thrown by the in-flight request (exactly the NPE this PR fixes) can be added after the assertion has already run, making the test pass even when the bug is present. Join the thread (with a timeout) before asserting. Additionally, if the thread hangs, it is left running as a non-daemon thread after the test.

findings.title: Created groups are not registered for cleanup
findings.body: The 100 groups created in `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` are only removed by the explicit delete loop. If `fail(...)` triggers or a delete throws, the remaining groups leak into the shared `managedRealm`, which can break other tests in the class (e.g. ones asserting group counts or names). Register each created group with `managedRealm.cleanup()` as other tests in this file do.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() may now return null, moving the NPE to callers
findings.body: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the group no longer exists in the store instead of throwing an NPE. Callers such as `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` pass the value straight to `GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(...)`, and other callers may unbox it to a primitive `long`, which would NPE again. The `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` contract does not document a nullable result. Returning `0L` (or delegating to the invalidation path via `getDelegateForUpdate()`) would be safer and keeps the API contract non-null.
